Multi-Cloud Library Management System Using Sidecar Data Plane

A multi-cloud library application using sidecar proxies for secure service communication, traffic management, health checking, and cross-cloud Redis caching.

AWS + GCP · Sidecar proxies · mTLS · Redis
01

Introduction

The project designs a Multi-Cloud Library Management System using a sidecar-based data plane and cross-cloud caching.

The library services are distributed across AWS and GCP. Each service has a sidecar proxy that manages service discovery, secure mTLS communication, traffic routing, health checking, retries and logging. A Redis cache layer is introduced between AWS and GCP to cache frequently accessed data such as book information and member information. This reduces repeated database requests, improves response time and reduces database load.

The system demonstrates

Multi-cloud deploymentServices distributed across AWS and GCP
Sidecar data planeIndependent proxy beside each service
Secure communicationService discovery and mTLS security
Traffic managementTraffic splitting, health checking and retries
Redis cachingFrequently requested data cached temporarily
Reliability & metricsFailure handling and performance benchmarking
02

Layer Descriptions

Client

The client sends requests such as:

  • View books
  • Register members
  • Borrow books
  • Return books

Library Services

There are three main services:

Book ServiceHandles book-related operations
Member ServiceHandles member information
Borrow ServiceHandles borrowing operations

Sidecar Proxy

Each service has its own sidecar proxy. The sidecar handles:

  • Service discovery
  • mTLS
  • Traffic routing
  • Health checks
  • Retries
  • Timeouts
  • Logging

Redis Cache

Redis stores frequently requested data temporarily. For example:

Book Service→Redis→Book data
Member Service→Redis→Member data

Instead of repeatedly accessing the database, services can retrieve frequently used information from Redis.

Control Plane

The control plane maintains:

  • Service locations
  • Health status
  • Traffic weights
  • Configuration
03

Implementation Plan

PhaseMilestoneEffort
Phase 1Basic Library ServicesLow
Phase 2Sidecar ProxyLow
Phase 3AWS + GCP DeploymentModerate
Phase 4mTLS, Discovery & Traffic SplittingModerate
Phase 5Redis Cross-Cloud CachingModerate
Phase 6Failure HandlingModerate
Phase 7Benchmarking & MetricsLow
Phase 1 – Basic Services

Create Book, Member and Borrow REST APIs and connect them to a simple database.

Phase 2 – Sidecar

Place a sidecar beside each service to forward requests and perform health checks.

Phase 3 – Multi-Cloud

Deploy services across AWS and GCP.

Client↓Sidecar↙ ↘AWSGCP→Book / Member
Phase 4 – Service Mesh Features

Implement service discovery to locate healthy services, mTLS to authenticate and encrypt service communication, and traffic splitting (for example, AWS 80% / GCP 20%).

Phase 5 – Cross-Cloud Caching

Implement Redis as a caching layer between AWS and GCP. Frequently accessed data such as book details, available books and member information will be cached.

Phase 6 – Failure Handling

Test service/sidecar failure, unhealthy instances, network delay and recovery. Redirect traffic to available services where possible.

Phase 7 – Benchmarking

Measure average latency, P95 latency, throughput, request success rate, traffic distribution, cache hit/miss rate, database request reduction and recovery time.

04

Feasibility

Technical: Node.js/Express, Docker, Redis, database and OpenSSL are sufficient to implement the library services, sidecar communication, mTLS and caching.

Implementation: Six independent phases make development and testing simple.

Resource: Development and testing can initially run locally using Docker.

Cloud: AWS and GCP can be used with free-tier/free-usage eligible resources.

Failure Testing: Containers can be stopped/restarted to simulate failures.

Cost: Open-source tools and free-tier resources are used; permanently running paid networking services are avoided.

Caching: Redis will be used through a free-tier/free-usage eligible or locally containerized setup during development to avoid unnecessary cloud costs.

The proposed development approach focuses on local Docker testing and free-tier/free-usage eligible cloud resources to avoid unnecessary costs.

06

Expected Outcome

The final system demonstrates how a library application can operate across multiple clouds while sidecars manage secure communication, service discovery, traffic routing and failure handling.

A Redis caching layer improves performance by serving frequently accessed data from the cache, reducing database load and repeated cross-cloud communication.
